full.description: This image is a photomicrograph of a tumor showing a distinct spindle cell proliferation. The neoplastic cells are arranged in a storiform or cartwheel pattern, characteristic of lesions such as dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans or malignant fibrous histiocytoma. The histological sections display hypercellular areas with interlacing fascicles of spindle-shaped cells. The morphology suggests a mesenchymal neoplasm with prominent storiform architecture.

blind.description: This image is a photomicrograph of a tumor tissue sample showing epithelial-like cells that line cleft-like spaces and gland-like structures, alongside areas with a fibrosarcoma-like spindle cell growth pattern. The microscopic findings reveal a biphasic architectural pattern characterized by both glandular and spindle cell components. These features are consistent with a malignant biphasic neoplasm, such as synovial sarcoma or a similar spindle cell tumor.

random.description: This image is a photomicrograph of tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin, likely depicting a neoplastic process. It shows a proliferation of spindle-shaped cells arranged in fascicles and whorled patterns, characteristic of a mesenchymal tumor such as a schwannoma or leiomyoma. The high-power view highlights cytologic features including elongated nuclei and varying cellularity. Histologic examination confirms the fibrous nature of the lesion.
